props.label: Why it works
props.description: A hero states the outcome, not the product, and offers a single next step. Everything else on the page exists to remove doubts before that step.

props.title: Who else uses this, in one glance
props.subtitle: Real customer logos, with permission, go here. No customers yet? Show partners, press or certifications instead — never invent them.

items.title: Before / after
items.text: One sentence that names the problem the customer had before and the result after. Specific numbers make it credible.
items.name: Customer name

items.title: The objection
items.text: A quote that answers the biggest objection your FAQ also answers: time to value, price or trust.
items.name: Customer name

items.title: A short one
items.text: Variety in length reads as authentic. Three quotes of identical shape read as written by the same person.
items.name: Customer name

props.note: Placeholders, on purpose: never publish invented testimonials. Ask three customers for one sentence each — what was hard before, what changed, and a number — and use their real name, role and photo with permission.

props.title: The six sections of a lead generation page
props.subtitle: Presence matters more than order: visitors scan, then read. Each block answers a question they have not asked yet.

items.title: A promise in the headline
items.description: Say what the visitor gets, in their words. “Get the checklist” beats “Download our PDF”. Keep the subtitle for the how and the who.

items.title: The offer, made concrete
items.description: Describe the magnet as a thing with a shape: pages, minutes, steps. Show it if you can. Vague value (“insights”) does not earn an email address.

items.title: Proof someone else trusted you
items.description: Logos, numbers or quotes. One real sentence from a customer outperforms three generic ones. Never invent them.

items.title: The form, short and visible
items.description: Ask only for what the follow-up needs. Say what happens after submit, and make the button describe the outcome, not the action.

items.title: Objections answered
items.description: An FAQ handles price, privacy, time and fit without a sales call — and doubles as structured data for search engines.

items.title: The same ask, repeated
items.description: Visitors who reached the end are the most convinced. Give them the same action, not a new one.

props.title: From click to conversation in four steps
props.subtitle: The page is one step of four. It only works when the ad before it and the email after it say the same thing.

items.title: Attract with one message
items.description: Every ad, post or email that points here says the same thing as the headline. Message match is the cheapest conversion lift available.

items.title: Remove friction
items.description: No menu, no footer full of links, a page that loads in under two seconds on mobile. This page keeps only a logo and one button in the header.

items.title: Capture the minimum
items.description: Two fields and a consent box. Progressive profiling can ask for more later, once the lead has a reason to answer.

items.title: Deliver instantly, follow up deliberately
items.description: Send the asset in the confirmation email, then a short sequence that earns the reply. The page’s job ends at submit; the sequence’s job starts there.

props.title: Asked before filling in a form
props.subtitle: Answering them here saves a sales call and gives search engines a rich result.

items.title: What is a lead generation landing page?
items.description: A single page with one goal: exchange something valuable — a guide, a demo, a quote, a trial — for a visitor’s contact details. Unlike a homepage it has no competing navigation and one call to action repeated throughout.

items.title: How many fields should the form have?
items.description: As few as your follow-up needs. Name and email are enough for a download; add company or budget only when sales will actually use them. Every extra required field lowers completion.

items.title: Above the fold or at the end?
items.description: Both, and the same offer. In the first screen for visitors who arrive convinced, repeated after the proof for those who need the full story. Two placements, one offer.

items.title: What is a good conversion rate?
items.description: It depends on the source. Cold paid traffic often converts in the low single digits; warm email or retargeting can reach 10–20%. Compare against your own baseline and change one thing at a time.

items.title: How do I make the form actually send submissions?
items.description: The form is a template. Point it at Netlify Forms, Formspree or your own endpoint; the fields, the consent box and the success message stay as they are.

items.title: Does this page work for GDPR / privacy consent?
items.description: The form ships with a consent checkbox linked to the privacy policy. Keep the label explicit about what you send and how often, and store the consent alongside the lead.
